item.title: Israelis denounce Trump’s deal with Iran
item.description: Israeli officials disparaged the peace deal and said Israel’s fight against Hezbollah in Lebanon would go on.

item.title: After news of Iran peace deal, Lebanese return home to assess wreckage
item.description: Some war-weary residents displaced from the south found relative quiet, with guarded optimism that Trump will pressure Israel to adhere to a truce.

item.title: Families of children killed in strike on Iranian school join leader’s funeral
item.description: In Iran, the school deaths have become a symbol for U.S.-Israeli brutality and an unjust war. The Washington Post is reporting from the country under restricted conditions.

item.title: Iran’s leader was killed in February. The country will finally bury him.
item.description: For the surviving Iranian regime, the funeral offers an opportunity to project power after withstanding months of war with Israel and the United States.

item.title: In Mideast and worldwide, cautious relief over deal to end damaging war
item.description: Some world leaders hailed the deal, but many in the Middle East were cautious, saying important details remain to be settled and warning the accord could easily fall apart.

item.title: Deadly Russian strikes hit Ukraine’s capital ahead of key NATO meeting
item.description: The overnight attacks on Kyiv killed at least 11 people as Russia stepped up a new offensive. Ukraine's president said NATO must do more to help his country intercept incoming missiles.

item.title: In Tehran, huge throngs mourn assassinated supreme leader Ali Khamenei
item.description: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who ruled over the Islamic Republic of Iran for 37 years, was killed along with several family members in an airstrike in February.
